title: Nightly sentinel ops playlist and deployment journal — 2026-06-12
content:
Purpose and context:
This doc is a compact, portable nightly ops 'playlist' that documents the cutover steps we actually ran for the June 12 private deployment rehearsal. It mixes checklist items, the incremental calendar we used for a phased canary, quick release notes, and a short deployment journal to capture surprises and follow-ups. Intended audience: release conductor, on-call SRE, patch owner, and the small ops squad running night shifts.

Goals for this run:
- Validate canary path across region-us-east-1 -> us-west-2 with progressive traffic shifts.
- Exercise the automatic fallback to model-quantized variants (q4-xx) when latency >75th percentile.
- Confirm telemetry gates (error-rate, p99 latency, request timeouts) are wired into alerts and rollout automation.
- Capture runbook gaps and list post-mortem actions.

Scope and constraints:
- Services in scope: serving-runtime, routing-service, kvcache, rollout-orchestrator.
- Not in scope: billing/usage-reporter, customer-console changes.
- Windows: night window 01:00-04:00 UTC to minimize customer impact.

High-level timeline (compact):
- 00:45 UTC: preflight checklist complete, engineer(s) on-call present.
- 00:50 UTC: annotate canary cohort in experiment system (cohort: 5% traffic us-east).
- 01:00 UTC: deploy model binary to canary pool (tag: release/2026.06.12-candidate).
- 01:10 UTC: smoke tests (gen, chat, embedding) run against canary instance.
- 01:20 UTC: promote to 25% if smoke green and p95 latency within thresholds.
- 01:40 UTC: monitor 25% for 20 mins. If p99 or error rate crosses gate -> automatic fallback; follow rollback checklist.
- 02:05 UTC: 50% if stable. Nightshift telemetry review.
- 02:40 UTC: full rollout to 100% in region if no regressions.

Preflight checklist (quick tick list for conductor) — must be green before 00:50:
- [ ] All PRs merged and CI green (PR: https://git.redwood.com/redwood/infra/pulls/2745).
- [ ] Release tag created and artifact uploaded to registry.
- [ ] Canary pool capacity verified (min 3 GPUs healthy).
- [ ] Smoke test vectors uploaded to /tmp/release-smokes/2026-06-12.
- [ ] Alerting runbooks pinned in Slack channel #release-nightrun-ops.
- [ ] Owner contact list updated (see collaborators).
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards pinned (links in linked artifacts).

Nightshift operational playlist (cheat-sheet):
- Start console: open serving runtime dashboard, routing heatmap, and KV cache hit-rate graph.
- Check SLO line: p95 latency < 280ms; if breached, flip canary to fallback variant.
- Watch for traffic teleport after 02:00 UTC (customer traffic spike window) — throttle if unknown surge.
- Keep Slack status: set to "on duty - release 2026.06.12".

Canary gating matrix (success criteria):
- Smoke tests: all must be PASS.
- Errors: 5xx < 0.05% over a 10-min window.
- p99 latency: within 2x baseline (baseline p99 recorded at 2026-06-08 run).
- Token drop / safety filter false positives: no increase >0.5% relative.

Rollback/fast-fail procedure (if any gate trips):
1) Immediately set rollout-orchestrator to fallback route A (degraded variant: model-q4m-2026-05).
2) Post message to #release-nightrun-ops with header "ROLLBACK EXECUTED" + reason + links to traces.
3) Snapshot logs and attach to ticket REL-2357.
4) If telemetry suggests persistent local infra problem (GPU OOM, disk pressure), escalate to infra@redwood and open incident.

Communication plan during run:
- Primary channel: #release-nightrun-ops (use thread per topic).
- Pager escalation: if rollback occurs, notify Release Manager (Michael Cheng) and SRE lead (Sofia Martinez).
- External comms: hold on customer-facing updates until post-mortem (unless user impact >1 hour).

Release notes draft (short, to be refined for customers):
- Release 2026-06-12 (internal codename: Nightly Sentinel)
- Primary changes: rollout of runtime kernel improvements to reduce memory churn and a new quantized model variant to improve cost per token.
- Expected impact: lower p95 token cost by ~4-6%, negligible change to latency for small prompts; improved stability for long-context workloads.
- Known limitations: fallback logic may increase variance temporarily during autoscale events; we will monitor closely and have a rollback ready.

Deployment journal — live notes (conductor entries):
- 00:47 UTC — preflight: CI shows intermittent flake on integration-test-03; reran and green (note: flaky test to be tracked, owner @Liam).
- 01:03 UTC — canary deploy started; initial smoke tests show embedding endpoint returning ~0.7% higher latency; within tolerance.
- 01:15 UTC — observed 503 spike for one canary instance (trace id T-6f8d3); instance recovered after restart; flagged as infra-ISP transient.
- 01:38 UTC — promoted to 25%; telemetry good except small KV cache miss rate increase (+2.2%).
- 02:02 UTC — 50% promotion; p99 trending upward but below threshold.
- 02:25 UTC — small routing flapping observed for sessions >2048 tokens; mitigated by temporarily pinning session affinity.
- 02:55 UTC — full rollout complete for region-us-east-1. No customer incidents reported during window.

Action items and follow-ups (who/what):
- [P1] Flaky integration-test-03 root cause and flakiness fix — owner: Liam O'Neill — target: 2026-06-18.
- [P2] Investigate KV cache miss regression under canary workload — owner: Sofia Martinez — add telemetry counter for TTL evictions.
- [P3] Session affinity improvement proposal for long-context sessions — owner: Michael Cheng — proto doc due 2026-06-20.
- [P4] Add explicit failure mode note to public release notes about temporary variance during autoscale — owner: product-hosted-api — target 2026-06-15.

Open questions (short list):
- Did the quantized fallback variant affect output quality for the small subset of evaluation prompts? Quick A/B on sampled logs needed.
- Should we expand night windows by 1 hour for next rehearsal to test high-concurrency ramp?
- Where to track the flaky integration tests long term: infra repo or test harness repo?

Useful links and refs (quick):
- PR: https://git.redwood.com/redwood/infra/pulls/2745
- Canary experiment: JIRA REL-2357
- Rollout automation job: infra/cron/rollout-nightly

Appendix: compact rollback checklist for shell operators (copyable):
- curl -X POST https://orchestrator.internal.redwood/api/v1/rollouts/abort -d '{"tag":"release/2026.06.12-candidate"}'
- kubectl scale deployment serving-runtime-canary --replicas=0 -n canary
- Start incident thread: /msg #release-nightrun-ops "ROLLBACK EXECUTED — see traces REL-2357"

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this short, make it consumable for the on-call — long essays don't help in the middle of a night run.
- We should convert the most-used steps into a tiny CLI helper (release-helper) so the conductor can avoid copy/paste mistakes.

End of journal.

Revision history:
- 2026-06-10: initial draft skeleton (Aditi Rao).
- 2026-06-11: added gating matrix, smoke vectors, and links (Michael Cheng).
- 2026-06-12: live notes appended after rehearsal; follow-ups assigned (Sofia Martinez).
